# layout: # STRUCTURE ONLY — containers and roots. Never file contents, never
# completeness. An operator who deleted a validator, edited a skill or removed
# a whole skill directory is using INSPIRE correctly; none of that may block an
# upgrade. Only the shape of the tree identifies a version's layout.
# NO COLUMN MAY EVER BE LEFT EMPTY — all four are mandatory on every row.
# verify_layout and layout_map both read a row with `IFS=$'\t' read -r layout
# musts nots dmap`, and bash treats tab as IFS whitespace no matter what else is
# in IFS, so it COLLAPSES a run of tabs instead of yielding an empty field. A row
# that left must_not_exist empty would therefore shift every later column left:
# dest_map would be read as `nots`, layout_map would return empty, and an upgrade
# would classify nothing, move nothing and still rewrite .inspire.lock — a silent
# no-op that claims success. A layout with nothing to require or nothing to forbid
# must say so with a path that cannot exist (e.g. `.inspire-no-such-marker`),
# never with an empty column.
# dest_map is where THIS layout materializes each base/ directory. It is what
# lets a manifest path be translated to its base/ counterpart, in either
# direction, without any inference: the base-relative middle (bin/…, hooks/…,
# skills/…, agents/…) is stable across every released version — only the roots
# moved.
# A NEW PAYLOAD CLASS IS NOT A NEW LAYOUT (decision, 0.9's base/agents/).
# `agents:.claude/agents` was added to the 0.3 row rather than opening a `0.9`
# row, and no 0.9.0 hop exists, because nothing MOVED — a hop's absence is the
# no-op. Three reasons, in order of force:
#   1. A second row would be UNDISCRIMINABLE. This file identifies a layout by
#      the SHAPE of the tree, and an additive class changes no shape: no root
#      moved, and `.claude/agents/` is a directory an operator may create or
#      delete freely, so its presence is not a legal marker (content markers are
#      forbidden here for the same reason). A `0.9` row could only reuse 0.3's
#      own markers, i.e. two layout ids verify_layout cannot tell apart.
#   2. It would make detect_version REFUSE REAL PROJECTS. A tie between two
#      manifests is resolved by taking the higher version when they share a
#      layout, and refused outright when they do not (lib/manifest.sh:114-129).
#      Give 0.9 its own layout id and any 0.9 project whose 0.8-era files are
#      all unmodified scores 100% against BOTH manifests, across layouts — an
#      upgrade refused with "proceeding would mean guessing". Under one layout
#      the same tie resolves to 0.9, which is the right answer.
#   3. The addition is inert for every past version. A dest_map entry is read
#      only by _middle/_from_middle (prefix translation) and by the two walkers
#      in lib/merge.sh, both of which skip an entry whose `base/<name>` is
#      absent. `.claude/agents` is a prefix no shipped manifest occupies and
#      that neither contains nor is contained by any other dest, so no path can
#      now translate that did not before, and the ten shipped manifests
#      reproduce byte-identically (plugin/test/manifest/03-reproduction-sweep.sh
#      proves it).
#      Nothing here is a presence or completeness check, so an operator who
#      deletes `.claude/agents/` still upgrades.
# The pre-0.3 row is deliberately NOT extended. That layout never materialized
# agents, and its dest_map is only ever read as a SOURCE map (TARGET_LAYOUT is
# 0.3), so an entry there would say a root pre-0.3 owned but never filled. The
# class still reaches a pre-0.3 project: classify's pass 2 and apply_base's
# pass 1 both walk the TARGET map, so base/agents/ arrives as a plain `create`.
pre-0.3
